rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names taught to Adam were the names of the things created on earth.
rows.anchor: يريد أسماء ما خلق في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God displayed the actual created beings to the angels and asked them to name them.
rows.anchor: أي عرض أعيان الخلق عليهم {فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel must fulfill the commands and prohibitions it had accepted from God.
rows.anchor: أوفوا لي بما قبلتموه من أمري ونهيي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will fulfill the reward He promised them for doing so.
rows.anchor: أوف لكم بما وعدتكم على ذلك من الجزاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets patience here as fasting.
rows.anchor: أي: بالصوم. في قول مجاهد (2) رحمه الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting and Ramadan are called patience because the faster restrains himself from food and drink.
rows.anchor: ويقال لشهر رمضان: شهر الصبر (3) ، وللصائم صابر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A restrained animal used as a target is called maṣbūra; patience shares the sense of holding something back.
rows.anchor: وكل من حبس شيئا فقد صبره. ومنه المصبورة التي نهي عنها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One is called patient in adversity because he restrains himself from despair.
rows.anchor: لأنه حبس نفسه عن الجزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fūm is said to mean wheat and bread.
rows.anchor: يقال: هو الحنطة، والخبز جميعا.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says fūm is an old dialect word in the command fūmū, meaning bake bread.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء (1) هي لغة قديمة يقول أهلها: فوموا، أي: اختبزوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes fūm to mean grains.
rows.anchor: ويقال: الفوم الحبوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba prefers garlic, supported by the reading thūmihā in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: وهذا أعجب الأقاويل إلي؛ لأنها في مصحف عبد الله: "وثومها"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garlic reading is linguistically supported by Arabic interchange of thāʾ and fāʾ, as in jadath/jadaf and mughāthīr/mughāfīr.
rows.anchor: والعرب تبدل الثاء بالفاء فيقولون جدث وجدف. والمغاثير والمغافير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāʾū means they returned; the verb is used as bǔtu bi-kadhā and abūʾu bihi, not bāʾa bi-l-shayʾ.
rows.anchor: أي رجعوا. يقال: بؤت بكذا فأنا أبوء به. ولا يقال: باء بالشيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasat means just and best; the cited verse uses it for the best and fairest person, and the poet describes people whose judgment others accept.
rows.anchor: أي: عدلا خيارا. ومنه قوله في موضع آخر: {قال أوسطهم ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was called the most distinguished of Quraysh in lineage; the best things are their middles, while excess and shortcoming are blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وأصل هذا أن خير الأشياء أوساطها، وأن الغلو والتقصير مذمومان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community is made witnesses over the people of earlier nations and their prophets.
rows.anchor: أي على الأمم المتقدمة لأنبيائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥṣār is a condition that prevents pilgrimage, such as illness, fracture, or an enemy; a person confined in prison or a house is instead described with ḥaṣara.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يعرض للرجل ما يحول بينه وبين الحج من مرض أو كسر (2) أو عدو.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form is aḥṣara iḥṣāran, so the pilgrim is muḥṣar; imprisonment is ḥuṣira and the person maḥṣūr.
rows.anchor: يقال: أحصر الرجل إحصارا فهو محصر. فإن حبس في سجن أو دار قيل: قد حصر فهو محصور.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The required offering is whatever is available and feasible; hady is an offering sent to the House, originally pronounced with a doubled yāʾ and then lightened.
rows.anchor: أي فما تيسر من الهدي وأمكن. والهدي ما أهدي إلى البيت. وأصله هدي مشدد فخفف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has shadda on the yāʾ in the phrase about the offering reaching its place; its singular is hadiyya, also lightened to hadya.
rows.anchor: وقد قرئ: (حتى يبلغ الهدي محله) بالتشديد (3) . واحده هدية. ثم يخفف فيقال: هدية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maḥill is the place where the offering becomes permissible for slaughter.
rows.anchor: والمحل: الموضع الذي يحل به نحره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about harm from the head means that the pilgrim shaved his head.
rows.anchor: أراد فحلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits fa-ḥalaqa, meaning he shaved, for brevity; Ibn Qutayba points to his work on difficult Qurʾanic expressions.
rows.anchor: فحذف "فحلق" اختصارا، على ما بينت في "تأويل المشكل"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nusuk here means slaughter; nasaktu li-llāh means I slaughtered for God.
rows.anchor: أي ذبح. يقال: نسكت لله، أي: ذبحت له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghw in an oath can mean words spoken without a deliberate oath.
rows.anchor: واللغو في اليمين: ما يجري في الكلام على غير عقد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view calls it an oath taken about something believed true that is actually false; God does not hold a person to it.
rows.anchor: ويقال: اللغو أن تحلف على الشيء ترى أنه كذلك وليس كذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God holds people to oaths their hearts deliberately intend when they know they are lying.
rows.anchor: بما تحلفون عليه وقلوبكم متعمدة، وتعلمون أنكم فيه كاذبون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naẓira means waiting or granting time to the debtor.
rows.anchor: أي انتظار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiving the debt owed by an insolvent person is better for the creditor.
rows.anchor: بما لكم على المعسر {خير لكم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ means fairness or equity; it also means the middle, since the middle is the fairest part.
rows.anchor: أي: نصف. يقال: دعاك إلى السواء أي إلى النصفة. وسواء كل شيء: وسطه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ka-ayyin means many.
rows.anchor: أي كثير من نبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribbiyyūn means large groups, and is also said to mean thousands; the word derives from ribba, a group, then forms a nisba and its plural.
rows.anchor: أي جماعات كثيرة. ويقال: الألوف. وأصله من الربة. وهي الجماعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahana means they did not weaken.
rows.anchor: {فما وهنوا} أي ضعفوا]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istanā means they did not humble or abase themselves; mustakīn derives from this sense.
rows.anchor: {وما استكانوا} ما خشعوا وذلوا. ومنه أخذ المستكين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mafāza means deliverance or escape from punishment; fāza means he was saved.
rows.anchor: أي بمنجاة ومنه يقال: فاز فلان أي نجا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Batha means that God spread people across the earth.
rows.anchor: أي نشر في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With accusative al-arḥāma, the command is to fear God and also fear severing family ties.
rows.anchor: من نصب أراد: اتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With genitive al-arḥāmi, the phrase means asking by God and by kinship, like swearing by God and kinship.
rows.anchor: ومن خفض أراد: الذي تساءلون به وبالأرحام (1) . وهو مثل قول الرجل: نشدتك بالله وبالرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥalāʾil of one's sons are the wives of one's sons.
rows.anchor: أزواج البنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Katabnā means We prescribed and imposed the obligation.
rows.anchor: أي: فرضنا عليهم وأوجبنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contracts are covenants; the poet al-Ḥuṭayʾa uses ʿaqadū for making a pact and reinforcing it.
rows.anchor: أي بالعهود. يقال: عقد لي عقدا أي جعل لي عهدا؛ قال الحطيئة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contracts are also said to be the obligations imposed on people.
rows.anchor: ويقال: هي الفرائض التي ألزموها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cattle category includes camels, cows, sheep, and wild animals.
rows.anchor: الإبل والبقر والغنم والوحوش كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception refers to the prohibited foods listed next, including carrion, blood, and pork.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي استثناه فقال: {حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of ḥurum is ḥarām; ḥarām and muḥrim have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: واحدهم حرام. والحرام والمحرم سواء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's shaʿāʾir are signs He established for obedience; shaʿīra is singular, and the ḥaram is an example.
rows.anchor: ما جعله علما لطاعته. واحدها شعيرة (3) مثل الحرم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on violating God's signs includes hunting in the sanctuary and similar acts.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا تحلوه فتصطادوا فيه، وأشباه ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred month is not to be violated by fighting.
rows.anchor: {ولا الشهر الحرام} فتقاتلوا فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hady is an offering sent to the House; its marking includes garlanding, covering, and piercing its hump, so it must not be made lawful before its destination.
rows.anchor: وهو ما أهدي إلى البيت. وهو من الشعائر. وإشعاره أن يقلد ويجلل ويطعن في سنامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qalāʾid were camels marked with bark from sanctuary trees so they would be safe wherever they traveled.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجل يقلد بعيره من لحاء شجر الحرم فيأمن بذلك حيث سلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āmīn al-bayt are those heading to the Sacred House; the singular is ām.
rows.anchor: يعني العامدين إلى البيت. واحدهم آم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking favor means seeking provision from God through trade, while seeking His approval is through pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: أي يريدون فضلا من الله، أي رزقا بالتجارة. {ورضوانا} بالحج.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people have left consecration, the command to hunt grants permission.
rows.anchor: أي خرجتم من إحرامكم. {فاصطادوا} على الإباحة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yajrimannakum means let it not cause you to commit a wrong; jārm can mean a person's breadwinner, and jarīmatuhum their earnings.
rows.anchor: أي لا يكسبنكم. يقال: فلان جارم أهله: أي كاسبهم. وكذلك جريمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hudhalī poet's line calls a bird's provision for its chick its earning, illustrating the root j-r-m.
rows.anchor: وقال الهذلي ووصف عقابا: جريمة ناهض في رأس نيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāhiḍ is the bird's chick; the mother earns and brings its food.
rows.anchor: والناهض: فرخها. يقول هي تكسب له وتأتيه بقوته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shanʾān means hatred; the command forbids hatred of people at the sanctuary from leading believers to violate its sanctity.
rows.anchor: أي: بغضهم يقال: شنأته أشنأه: إذا أبغضته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hatred of those who barred access to the sanctuary must not lead to transgression against its inviolability.
rows.anchor: لا يحلمنكم بغض قوم نازلين بالحرم على أن تعتدوا فتستحلوا حرمة الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jawāriḥ are hunting dogs; the root ijti rāḥ means earning or acquiring, as in a woman having no provider and what you acquire.
rows.anchor: كلاب الصيد. وأصل الاجتراح: الاكتساب. يقال: امرأة لا جارح لها، أي: لا كاسب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukallibīn means people who own or handle dogs.
rows.anchor: أصحاب كلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-naʿam usually means camels, though it can also include cows and sheep.
rows.anchor: و (النعم) الإبل. وقد تكون البقر والغنم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdl dhālika ṣiyāman means an equivalent amount in fasting.
rows.anchor: {أو عدل ذلك صياما} أي مثله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God imposed mercy on Himself for His creatures.
rows.anchor: أي: أوجبها على نفسه لخلقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about those who lost themselves refers back to the command to travel and observe the outcome of the deniers.
rows.anchor: هذا مردود إلى قوله: {قل سيروا في الأرض ثم انظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-lawlā is a rebuke meaning why did they not humble themselves when God's punishment came?
rows.anchor: أي فهلا إذ جاءهم بأسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghtatan means suddenly, in an open and face-to-face manner.
rows.anchor: فجأة وجهرة معاينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mublisūn means despairing, with their hands thrown down in helplessness.
rows.anchor: يائسون ملقون بأيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dābir is the last or remaining part of a people, as in saying their root was uprooted.
rows.anchor: أي آخرهم. كما يقال: اجتث أصلهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istahwathu means the devils drove him away and took him off course.
rows.anchor: أي: هوت به وذهبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr; his companions calling him back to guidance were his father and mother.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر (4) . وأصحابه: أبوه وأمه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils whisper into the hearts of their allies that they should dispute with the believers.
rows.anchor: أي: يقذفون في قلوبهم أن يجادلوكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is God's religion, and Satan means to turn people away from it.
rows.anchor: أي: دينك. يقول: لأصدنهم عنه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgetting them means leaving or abandoning them.
rows.anchor: أي: نتركهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bushran is as if the winds give good news; God's mercy here is rain, called mercy because it comes through His mercy.
rows.anchor: كأنها تبشر. ورحمته ها هنا: المطر، سماه رحمة: لأنه كان برحمته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading nushuran, the word means either plural nushūr or something scattered; the idiom asks God to gather one's scattered affairs.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأها (نشرا بين يدي رحمته) أراد جمع نشور ونشر الشيء ما تفرق منه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqallat means the clouds carried or bore water; istiqlāl is used for what one carries.
rows.anchor: أي حملت. ومنه يقال: ما أستقل به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ means the chiefs and notables; the term has that meaning wherever it occurs.
rows.anchor: أشرافهم ووجوههم. وكذلك الملأ من قومه [في كل موضع]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When anger fell silent from Moses, it means that his anger subsided.
rows.anchor: أي: سكن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuskhatihā means what was copied or transcribed from the tablets.
rows.anchor: أي: فيما نسخ منها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses chose from among his people; min is omitted, as in the idiom I chose you, the people, meaning from the people.
rows.anchor: أي: اختار من قومه. فحذف "من" والعرب تقول: اخترتك القوم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudnā means we repented and returned to You; the related name for Jews reflects returning from one thing to another.
rows.anchor: أي: تبنا إليك. ومنه: {ومن الذين هادوا} (3) كأنهم رجعوا عن شيء إلى شيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dharāʾnā means We created; dhurriyya is connected with creation, and most Arabs omit the hamza.
rows.anchor: أي خلقنا لجهنم. ومنه ذرية الرجل: إنما هي الخلق. ولكن همزها يتركه أكثر العرب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of God's beautiful names are al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, and al-ʿAzīz.
rows.anchor: أي: الرحمن والرحيم والعزيز. وأشباه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād in God's names is deviation from truth, such as calling idols al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt; laḥd is named for a grave's side.
rows.anchor: أي: يجورون عن الحق ويعدلون. فيقولون: اللات والعزى ومناة، وأشباه ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzīz ʿalayhi means it is painful or severe for him when hardship and harm befall you.
rows.anchor: أي: شديد عليه ما أعنتكم وضركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two of every pair means one male and one female.
rows.anchor: أي من كل ذكر وأنثى اثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means those whom the decree of destruction had already overtaken.
rows.anchor: أي سبق القول بهلكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majrāhā means the ship's course or journey.
rows.anchor:
مجراها} مسيرها.
{ومرساها} حيث ترسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marsāhā means where it is moored or comes to rest; the related verb can also mean to stop.
rows.anchor: حيث ترسى وترسو أيضا. أي: تقف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muʿaqqibāt are angels who follow one another through the night and day, one group succeeding another.
rows.anchor: يعني: ملائكة يعقب بعضها بعضا في الليل والنهار، إذا مضى فريق خلف بعده فريق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels guard the person by God's command.
rows.anchor: أي: بأمر الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāl means protector, comparable to the paired forms qādir/qadīr and ḥāfiẓ/ḥafīẓ.
rows.anchor: أي: ولي. مثل: قادر وقدير. وحافظ وحفيظ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The days of God are the days of His blessings.
rows.anchor: أي: بأيام النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the routes is a deviating path on which people are not guided; jāʾir means turning away from the straight course.
rows.anchor: أي: من الطرق جائر لا يهتدون فيه. والجائر: العادل عن القصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāṣiban means continuous or perpetual; dīn here means obedience.
rows.anchor: أي: دائما (3) . والدين: الطاعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every obedience owed to another ends through disappearance or death, whereas obedience to God endures.
rows.anchor: ليس من أحد يدان له ويطاع إلا انقطع ذلك عنه بزوال أو هلكة، غير الله. فإن الطاعة تدوم له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's waḥy to the bee means either inspiring it or subjecting it; waḥy can occur through speech, indication, or subjection.
rows.anchor: أي: ألهمها. وقيل:] سخرها. وقد بينت في كتاب "المشكل" أنه قد يكون كلاما وإشارة وتسخيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything raised or trellised, such as a vine, plant, or roof, is an ʿarsh or maʿrūsh.
rows.anchor: كل شيء عرش من كرم أو نبات أو سقف: فهو عرش ومعروش.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull in eat from all fruits is not universal and means fruits generally; the same limited use occurs in the statement that the wind destroyed everything.
rows.anchor: أي: من الثمرات. وكل هاهنا ليس على العموم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhululan means submissive and guided under God's subjection; it is the plural of dhalūl.
rows.anchor: أي: منقادة بالتسخير. وذلل: جمع ذلول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anʿum is the plural of naʿm, as in a day of prosperity and a day of adversity, whose plurals are anʿum and abʾus.
rows.anchor: جمع نعم. يقال: يوم نعم ويوم بؤس، ويجمع أنعم وأبؤس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba rejects the claim that anʿum is the plural of niʿma, because faʿla does not pluralize on the afʿul pattern.
rows.anchor: وليس قول من قال: إنه جمع نعمة بشيء؛ لأن فعلة لا يجمع على أفعل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets istawā as rising above, as in being above an animal or a house.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: علا. قال: وتقول استويت فوق الدابة، واستويت فوق البيت.

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another interpreter takes istawā to mean settled, citing Noah's settling in the ark and Moses reaching maturity and settling.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: استوى: استقر. واحتج بقول الله عز وجل: {فإذا استويت أنت ومن معك على الفلك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave each kind of creature its matching form, including a male its corresponding female.
rows.anchor: أي أعطى كل ذكر خلقا مثله من الإناث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then guided the male to approach the female.
rows.anchor: أي هدى الذكر لإتيان الأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā bālu means what is their condition or state, as in the idiom may God set your state aright.
rows.anchor: أي فما حالها؟ يقال: أصلح الله بالك؛ أي حالك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nuhā means intellects, and nahya means reason; Dhū al-Rumma's poetic phrase dhī nihya describes a person of understanding.
rows.anchor: لذي نهية إلا إلى أم سالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawā means perished; the idiom hawat ummuhu means he was destroyed.
rows.anchor: أي هلك. يقال: هوت أمه. أي هلكت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no deviation from the summoner and no turning aside in following him.
rows.anchor: أي لا يعدلون عنه ولا يعرجون في اتباعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The voices became subdued or quiet.
rows.anchor:
الأصوات} أي خفيت.
{فلا تسمع إلا همسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hams is a faint sound, such as the sound of footsteps.
rows.anchor: أي إلا صوتا خفيا. يقال: هو صوت الأقدام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement puts the Prophet and his opponents on equal knowledge: he has informed them and openly declared hostility.
rows.anchor: أعلمتكم وصرت أنا وأنتم على سواء، وإنما يريد نابذتكم وعاديتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This compressed expression means that he has informed both sides, making their knowledge equal.
rows.anchor: وأعلمتكم ذلك، فاستوينا في العلم. وهذا من المختصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣawāff describes camels standing with their forelegs joined when they are prepared for slaughter.
rows.anchor: أي قد صفت أيديها. وذلك إذا قرنت أيديها عند الذبح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajabat junūbuhā means their sides fell to the ground; the same verb describes the sun setting.
rows.anchor: أي سقطت. ومنه يقال: وجبت الشمس: إذا غابت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qāniʿ is a beggar; qaniʿa can mean asking, while qanaʿa means being content.
rows.anchor: السائل (1) . يقال: قنع يقنع قنوعا؛ ومن الرضا قنع يقنع قناعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muʿtar is someone who visits or approaches hoping for a gift without asking; several forms of the verb are used.
rows.anchor: الذي يعتريك: أي يلم بك لتعطيه ولا يسأل. يقال: اعترني وعرني، وعراني واعتراني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn here means reckoning; Ibn Qutayba says the word dīn has multiple senses discussed in his work on difficult Qurʾanic expressions.
rows.anchor: الدين هاهنا الحساب. والدين يتصرف على وجوه قد بينتها في كتاب "المشكل"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants are specially ascribed to the Merciful because He chose them, even though all people are His servants, like the House and she-camel of God.
rows.anchor: -والناس جميعا عبيده-: [لاصطفائه] إياهم. كما يقال: "بيت الله" -والبيوت كلها لله-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawnan means walking gently or calmly on earth.
rows.anchor: أي مشيا رويدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salāman means sound and decent speech, free of obscenity and foul language.
rows.anchor: أي سدادا من القول: لا رفث فيه، ولا هجر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rasūl can be singular in form but collective in meaning, like ḍayf for guests and ṭifl for children.
rows.anchor: الرسول يكون بمعنى الجميع، كما يكون الضيف.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says rasūl can mean risāla, a message; the poet's line uses rasūl in that sense.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: "رسول بمعنى: رسالة". وأنشد: لقد كذب الواشون;

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets al-ḍāllīn as people who forgot, citing the verse that a woman may forget and another remind her.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة (5) "يعني من الناسين". واستشهد بقوله عز وجل في موضع آخر: {أن تضل إحداهما}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound heart is one free from associationism.
rows.anchor: أي خالص من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karīm is said to mean noble because of the sender's nobility.
rows.anchor: أي شريف: بشرف صاحبه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the letter is noble because it bears a seal.
rows.anchor: ويقال: بالخاتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿlū ʿalayya means do not act arrogantly toward me; it derives from rising above.
rows.anchor: من "العلو": أي لا تتكبروا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time described as a moment of heedlessness is said to be midday.
rows.anchor: يقال: نصف النهار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man from Moses' faction was one of his companions, namely an Israelite.
rows.anchor: أي من أصحابه. يعني: بني إسرائيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man's enemy was among Moses' enemies; ʿaduww can refer to one person or a group.
rows.anchor: أي من أعدائه. و "العدو" يدل على الواحد، وعلى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakaza means struck or pushed, like the related verbs lakaza, nakaza, nahaza, and lahaza.
rows.anchor: أي لكزه. يقال وكزته ولكزته [ونكزته ونهزته] ولهزته؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaḍā ʿalayhi means killed him; qaḍaytu ʿalayhi can mean I finished or settled it.
rows.anchor: أي قتله. وكل شيء فرغت منه: فقد قضيته، وقضيت عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traces of God's mercy are the traces of rain.
rows.anchor: يعني: آثار المطر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ṣalāt upon believers means He blesses them, and it is also said to mean He forgives them.
rows.anchor: أي يبارك عليكم. ويقال: يغفر لكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' ṣalāt means that they ask forgiveness for the believers.
rows.anchor: أي تستغفر لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting is spoken to the people of Paradise as if they hear it directly from a merciful Lord.
rows.anchor: أي سلام يقال لهم [فيها] كأنهم يتلقونه من رب رحيم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant means: did I not command and instruct you, or charge you?
rows.anchor: ألم آمركم ألم أوصكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their azwāj are their counterparts; Arabs say they paired camels by joining one to another.
rows.anchor: أي أشكالهم. تقول العرب: زوجت إبلي؛ إذا قرنت واحدا بآخر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes their partners to be their companion devils.
rows.anchor: ويقال: (6) قرناؤهم من الشياطين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight pairs of livestock are eight kinds, those named by God in Sūrat al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: أي ثمانية أصناف، وهي التي ذكرها الله -عز ذكره- في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation in stages means a clinging form after a drop, then a lump after the clinging form.
rows.anchor: أي علقة بعد نطفة ومضغة بعد علقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three darknesses are said to be the placenta, womb, and abdomen.
rows.anchor: يقال (5) : ظلمة المشيمة وظلمة الرحم وظلمة البطن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inherited earth is the land of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي أرض الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natabawwaʾu means we settle or dwell in Paradise wherever we wish.
rows.anchor: أي ننزل منها {حيث نشاء}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say God is their Lord and then remain upright believe and persist in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: أي آمنوا، ثم استقاموا على طاعة الله.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet exhorts people to remain upright, while saying they will not manage to do so exhaustively.
rows.anchor: قال النبي -صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم- (3) : " استقيموا ولن تحصوا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jawārī in the sea are ships.
rows.anchor: يعني: السفن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aʿlām means mountains, and ʿalam is its singular.
rows.anchor: أي الجبال. واحدها: علم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawākid means still or motionless on the surface of the sea.
rows.anchor: أي سواكن على ظهر البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāthiya describes people kneeling on their knees, in a state of unease rather than security.
rows.anchor: [باركة] (5) على الركب. يراد: أنها غير مطمئنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being called to one's book means being called to one's reckoning.
rows.anchor: أي إلى حسابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record seems to speak because people read it, recognize what it indicates, and are reminded by it.
rows.anchor: يريد: أنهم يقرءونه فيدلهم ويذكرهم؛ فكأنه ينطق عليهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nastansikhu means We write down or record.
rows.anchor: إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون} أي نكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother's burden and delivery in hardship mean she undergoes difficulty in both stages.
rows.anchor: {حملته أمه كرها} أي مشقة. {ووضعته كرها} أي مشقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awziʿnī means inspire me; the root īzāʿ originally means urging someone toward something, as in being devoted to it.
rows.anchor: أي ألهمني. والأصل في "الإيزاع": الإغراء بالشيء؛ يقال: فلان موزع بكذا ومولع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fataḥnā means We decreed a great decree; al-Fattāḥ is a name for a judge.
rows.anchor: أي قضينا لك قضاء عظيما. ويقال للقاضي: الفتاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn here means recompense for deeds and requital; the verb can mean to repay someone for what he did.
rows.anchor: يعني الجزاء بالأعمال والقصاص. ومنه يقال: دنته بما صنع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists treated al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt as daughters of God, so the passage challenges them for assigning Him females while claiming males for themselves.
rows.anchor: كانوا يجعلونها بنات الله؛ فقال: ألكم الذكور من الولد وله الإناث؟!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulṭān means proof or evidence.
rows.anchor: ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان} أي حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the soul reaches the throat is the meaning of the expression about reaching the throat.
rows.anchor: أي فهلا إذا بلغت النفس الحلقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr madīnīn means not owned or subjugated, deriving from dāna lahu bi-l-ṭāʿa, to obey him.
rows.anchor: أي غير مملوكين أذلاء (2) . من قولك: دنت له بالطاعة.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets madīnīn as people being recompensed.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: {مدينين} مجزيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarjiʿūnahā means return the soul.
rows.anchor: {ترجعونها} أي تردون النفس!.
